items.stem: What is OneLake in Microsoft Fabric?

options.text: A single, tenant-wide logical data lake that serves all Fabric workloads
options.rationale: Correct: OneLake is the unified store built into every Fabric tenant.

options.text: A separate storage account you must provision per workload
options.rationale: OneLake is built in and shared, not provisioned per workload.
OneLake is storage, not a report type.
OneLake is a cloud SaaS data lake on ADLS Gen2.

items.explanation: Correct: OneLake is the unified store built into every Fabric tenant.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about lakehouse and warehouse in Fabric are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Both store data in Delta format on OneLake and share the same SQL engine
options.rationale: Correct: both use Delta on OneLake and a common SQL engine.

options.text: A lakehouse suits Spark-based data engineering with structured and unstructured data
options.rationale: Correct: the lakehouse is built for Spark and mixed data types.

options.text: A warehouse requires copying data out of OneLake first
options.rationale: The warehouse stores data in OneLake in Delta format, no copy required.

options.text: A lakehouse cannot be queried with T-SQL at all
options.rationale: A lakehouse exposes a SQL analytics endpoint for T-SQL queries.

items.explanation: Correct: both use Delta on OneLake and a common SQL engine.

items.stem: In the Fabric hierarchy, which is correct from top to bottom?

options.text: Tenant, then workspaces, then items such as lakehouses
options.rationale: Correct: a tenant contains workspaces, which contain items.
That ordering is wrong; the tenant is at the top.
The tenant is above the workspace, not below.
A lakehouse is an item inside a workspace inside a tenant.
